doc.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Cab's rhythm section, Mingus, marriage and the band's end
title: O.C. Johnson, studio drummer, friend and neighbor
summary: Hinton tells how O.C. Johnson got work on a date by speaking up mid-take and became a close friend who bought a house on the next block.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: O.C. Johnson, we grew up together in Washington, D.C. As a matter of fact, he was the original drummer… just before the taping we were looking at something from The Subject Is Jazz. O.C. was the original drummer on that show.
Because as you say, he could do anything.
I mean whatever you needed, he could do it.

He was there. [Unintelligible]. He was so beautiful about friendship. I was already in the business, recording and Joe Jones was [unintelligible]. We had gotten to the New York Rhythm Section but we were doing things, but Joe didn‟t have the charisma to conform to all the different things. We did a date for somebody and O.C. came in town with Earl Hines and we invited him down to the date to see it and he [unintelligible] and when we finished the date just as that‟s noted, O.C. said, “Oh, yeah”. We said, “Oh, man, don‟t do that, you‟ve got to wait”. He said, “oh, I‟m sorry”. The producers, they said keep that in [laughter]. It sounded great on there and they passed him a withholding slip so he got paid for it

And from then on O.C. had the dates and he was just wonderful. We had just gotten our first Chevrolet. Mona had gotten a Chevrolet to haul me back and forth for the record dates and when Joe said go and just take O.C., so we brought O.C. in the car to take him where we were going because our dates were more or less the same. And O.C. told Mona, he said Mona, I see Mr. [Unintelligible] give me some money. You ain‟t going to have to come get Milt anymore, I‟ll take him home. So a little time later somebody… O.C. bought a Cadillac for $300 [laugher] and we were

[unintelligible] and O.C…. we get in his car coming down Queens Boulevard, we pushed it more then we rode it [laughter]. That thing kept stopping. We had to push to the next station. One of the first things… O.C. got a good car, got him a real Cadillac and sure enough she didn‟t have to come for me anymore. He took me and brought me home. In fact we were so close, he bought his house right out here near me on the next block and his wife is still there.
